clue.text: Concept, but ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of places the word for but in front of the abbreviation for time

parts.note: though can mean but, as in 'small though it is'

explanation.surface: An idea that someone had before its time.
explanation.definitionFit: A concept is an idea, as is a thought, the noun meaning something conceived in the mind.

clue.text: Company or body of soldiers, from what we hear

indicators.note: what we hear points to a word said out loud that is written differently

parts.note: a troop is a unit of soldiers

explanation.surface: Gossip about a company or a unit of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical company of performers who tour together is called by this word.

clue.text: Unique type of switch saving energy

indicators.note: saving here means keeping inside, so the switch word holds the next letter

parts.note: an on-off switch has two positions
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A rare kind of switch that saves energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made or done only once, without repeat, is unique.

clue.text: Move ahead before second eleven gradually gain more impetus

indicators.note: before places the first pair of pieces in front of the rest

parts.note: get as in 'get going' or 'get out', to move
up means ahead, as in a goal up
a team of eleven players, as in football or cricket

explanation.surface: A second-string side gradually builds up momentum on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second eleven' reads as a reserve team; it splits into second (S) and eleven (TEAM).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from steam engines building pressure, so it means gathering speed or energy slowly.

clue.text: Flower you and I name first

indicators.note: first means the word for name comes ahead of the word for you and I

parts.note: a tag is a name or label
us is you and I together

explanation.surface: You and I put the flower's name first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick: something that flows, a river. The Tagus runs through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows, so crosswords call it a flower; the Tagus is the longest river of Iberia.

clue.text: Johnny-come-lately's winning jump

parts.note: up means winning, as a team two goals up
to start is to jump with surprise

explanation.surface: A newcomer's leap that brings victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A Johnny-come-lately is a recent arrival who gets above themselves, a newcomer made good too fast.

clue.text: Secret Service?

definitions.meaning: secret in the sense of sly or done deceitfully
a serve in tennis or a delivery bowled with the hand below shoulder level

explanation.surface: The Secret Service, a security agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret Service' reads as the spy agency; it splits into sly and a low-handed delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sly or deceitful, and also describes a ball delivered with the hand below the shoulder.

clue.text: Large number left secure

parts.note: a sea of faces is a large number of them

explanation.surface: A big crowd was left safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal a container or deal is to close it firmly, to make it secure.

clue.text: Strong cat, lithe, jumping

indicators.note: jumping letters leap out of place into a new order

explanation.surface: A powerful, supple cat leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletic person is fit and muscular, physically strong.

clue.text: US actor, Ben, having blown top, strangles her heartlessly in suspense film?

indicators.note: strangles means the shortened surname grips the other piece inside it
having blown top means the opening letter of the actor's surname is gone

parts.note: Ben Stiller is an American actor

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of her is taken out

explanation.surface: An actor loses his temper and throttles a woman in a tense film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown top' suggests the actor losing his temper, but 'having blown top' leaves TILLER, 'heartlessly' leaves HR, and 'strangles' wraps the first round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a tense film or novel built on suspense, so a suspense film is an example.

clue.text: Open at an end? Head for Turnberry

parts.note: something over is finished, at an end

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of Turnberry

explanation.surface: A golfer asks if play is finished and makes for Turnberry, a Scottish course that hosts the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like the golf championship played at Turnberry, a links course in Ayrshire, Scotland; it is the adjective meaning unconcealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is done in plain view, not hidden; an open act is a public one.

clue.text: Sponsor priest on trail going west

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another follows it
in an across answer, going west means reading right to left, so the word for trail runs backwards

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail them
Father is the title of a Catholic priest

explanation.surface: A sponsor priest walking a trail westward.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at baptism, vouching for its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Praise the old man's attempt to make sausage rolls ingredient?

parts.note: to puff a product is to praise it extravagantly
the old man is father, pa, so his is pa's
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone praises Dad's effort at baking sausage rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: this flaky pastry is one ingredient of sausage rolls, among other uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage rolls are sausage meat wrapped in a light, flaky, layered dough, so that dough is one of their ingredients.

clue.text: Fit? Quite possibly

definitions.meaning: fit in the sense of healthy, in good health
as in 'it may ... rain', meaning it quite possibly will

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they are fit and answers that they quite possibly are.
explanation.definitionFit: Well means in good health, and as an adverb it softens a guess to likely, as in 'may well'.

clue.text: Desert Italian abroad? Don't do that

parts.note: to desert is to leave
out can mean abroad, away from home, as in 'out in India'

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to abandon an Italian overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase is a plea to stop, a request not to do or say something.

clue.text: Prevent attendant getting prison sentence in final part of play

parts.note: to stop something is to prevent it
a page is a young attendant
time is slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: Stopping a servant from going to jail at the end of a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests a stage drama; it is a football match, where extra minutes are added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, minutes added at the end of each half for injuries and delays are the closing period of play.

clue.text: Papers carried by current head of state

indicators.note: carried by means the papers sit inside the word for current

parts.note: present means current, existing now
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: A current head of state's documents.
explanation.definitionFit: In a republic the elected leader at the top of the state holds this title.

clue.text: A loud female during lecture must leave platform

indicators.note: during means these pieces come in the middle of the word for lecture

parts.note: to lecture someone is to scold them
F is forte, the musical notation for loud

explanation.surface: A noisy woman interrupting a lecture has to quit the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised wooden platform, once used for executions, or a structure builders work on.

clue.text: Seafood board not put up?

parts.note: a plank is a long board

indicators.note: in a down answer, put up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A seafood platter that isn't put up on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seafood' looks like fish for dinner; it is food for whales, the floating mass of tiny organisms in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are drifting tiny organisms that many sea creatures eat, so they are literally food in the sea.

clue.text: Bird caught next to Peak District river

indicators.note: next to sets the river's name beside the word for caught, after it

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to catch or arrest them
the Dove is a river in the Peak District, a national park in central England

explanation.surface: A bird caught beside a river in the Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common grey-buff species of pigeon with a black neck band, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Air in small coach

parts.note: to coach someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Fresh air inside a small coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' suggests the atmosphere; it is a tune, as in a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music or melody, as is an air, so both mean a tune.

clue.text: Heart and clubs put down picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the letters are said out loud and written as another word

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs; to enter details is to put them down in writing

explanation.surface: A card player puts down hearts and clubs, then picks them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' and 'clubs' suggest card suits; the heart is the definition, a core.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its middle or core, as in the heart of the city.

clue.text: Good penalty

definitions.meaning: good in the sense of satisfactory, all right
a sum of money paid as a punishment

explanation.surface: A penalty that turns out to be a good one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for satisfactory and a noun for a monetary punishment.

clue.text: New hit list prepared? Blow me!

indicators.note: a list prepared anew is drawn up again, its letters set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at a freshly prepared hit list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow me!' reads as an exclamation of surprise, but it is the instrument speaking: you blow into it to play it.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny whistle is a small wind instrument played by blowing, so it could say 'Blow me'.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed, a wife over boot

indicators.note: over means turned over, so in this down answer the pieces read upwards

parts.note: an embarrassed face turns red

explanation.surface: A wife is shamefaced over a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wader is a tall waterproof boot worn by anglers to stand in rivers.

clue.text: Basil, perhaps, in another book

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words another book

explanation.surface: Basil, perhaps a character, appearing in another book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' reads as a man's name; it is the plant used in cooking, an example signalled by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a fragrant culinary plant, one example of the leafy flavourings cooks use.

clue.text: Getting better, continuously swallowing them

indicators.note: swallowing means the phrase for continuously takes the next word inside it

parts.note: on end means without a break, as in 'for hours on end'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone constantly swallowing them, perhaps pills, while getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' signals the containment; 'on end' is the idiom for without a break, as in 'for hours on end'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the mend is to be recovering, getting better after illness or trouble.

clue.text: Style of painting embraced by Picasso particularly

indicators.note: embraced by means the letters sit held within the words Picasso particularly

explanation.surface: A painting style Picasso especially took up.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s abstract style using patterns that create optical illusions of movement.

clue.text: Eccentric daughter in golf club

parts.note: Golf is the NATO alphabet word for G
a bat is a club used to hit a ball

explanation.surface: An odd daughter in a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' reads as one thing; it splits into golf (G) and club (BAT).
explanation.definitionFit: A dingbat is an informal name for a strange or foolish person, a crank.

clue.text: Train European element in Parisian's street

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the French word for street

parts.note: rue is French for street, as a Parisian would say
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A train with a European element arriving in a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train; it is a noun for a band of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can be the group of attendants following an important person, their entourage.
